title: {{NAME}} and the Light Bringers
moral: Light takes many forms, and all of them matter.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a shimmering white hero suit with gold and fairy-light details, white boots, and a golden cape — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
There was a district of the city that had been without proper lighting for three months.

The power infrastructure was complex, the repair timeline was long, and the residents had been living by candlelight and battery lamps.

The major hero squads were on bigger assignments.

{{NAME}} visited the district and came home and called in two favours.

Favour one: the fairy council, who could produce sustained bio-luminescent light under certain conditions.

Favour two: Meridian, a unicorn whose horn could channel ambient energy into usable light.

Between three of them: enough to light a district.

pages.content:
The fairy council provided floating light colonies: clusters of their natural glow, sustained by collective magical effort, hung at street lamp height throughout the district.

Meridian walked the main street each evening and at her presence, ambient energy converted to warm glow: the district's emergency battery lights brightened, the street-level illumination increased, her horn's radius extending warmth for sixty metres in each direction.

{{NAME}} coordinated placement, maintenance schedules, and communication with residents.

Day one: the district had light again.

pages.content:
The district residents began leaving things for the fairies: small dishes of honey, flower arrangements, sugar water in tiny cups. The fairies maintained the light colonies more brightly in response.

Children left paper drawings for Meridian, placed where she would walk. She stopped at each one.

{{NAME}} kept the coordination running, troubleshooting when a fairy colony dimmed or Meridian's route needed adjusting.

For six weeks, the district was the best-lit area in the city.

The infrastructure repair team arrived finally and found people who had learned to give and receive care from unexpected sources.

pages.content:
The official lights came back on in week seven.

The fairies held their colonies one extra night, a farewell.

Meridian walked the main street for the last time and the existing street lamps stayed lit even after her horn's range ended, as though they had been tuned to a new brightness.

{{NAME}} watched from a corner.

The district's residents were outside: standing at their doors, watching the transition from temporary light to permanent light, not rushing in.

Savouring it.

pages.content:
He walked home through the lit city, the district behind him full of ordinary electricity.

But better than before. He knew it was better, though nothing had changed technically.

The people in it had learned something about receiving care.

And the fairies and Meridian had learned something about the city.

In bed, he lay in the warm dark and thought about all the kinds of light there were.

He closed his eyes.

Somewhere in the city, a district was still slightly brighter than the engineering explained.
